records.source: Ἀγρίππας δὲ πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον ἔφη· Ἐπιτρέπεταί σοι ὑπὲρ σεαυτοῦ λέγειν.
records.gloss: Agrippa then to Paul said: It is permitted to you for yourself to speak.
pieces: Agrippa said to Paul, "You have permission to speak on your own behalf."

L.1: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "It is permitted for you to speak for yourself."

R.1: King Agrippa said to Paul, "You may now speak for yourself."

decisions.choice: Agrippa: King Herod Agrippa II
decisions.reason: Agrippa I died in 12:23. His son Agrippa II ruled lands north and east of Galilee under Rome and had charge of the temple and the choice of the high priest, as Josephus records. He came with Bernice to greet Festus (25:13).

decisions.choice: to speak for yourself: to speak in your own defense
decisions.reason: The phrase is the language of a hearing. Paul at once begins his defense (26:1-2).

decisions.choice: King Agrippa
decisions.reason: Readable adds his title so a new reader knows who he is.

records.heading: Paul makes his defense before Agrippa

records.source: τότε ὁ Παῦλος ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπελογεῖτο·
records.gloss: Then Paul, having stretched out the hand, began his defense:
pieces: So Paul held out his hand and began to make his defense:

L.1: Then Paul stretched out [his] hand and began his defense:

R.1: Paul raised his hand and began to defend himself.

decisions.choice: stretched out his hand: the gesture of a speaker beginning an address
decisions.reason: Speakers in the Greek and Roman world opened with a raised hand. Paul is in chains (26:29), yet he takes the speaker's stance. Elsewhere a raised hand asks for silence (13:16, 21:40).

decisions.choice: began his defense: a formal reply to charges
alternatives: an argument for the faith in general
decisions.reason: The verb is the word for a defense in court, as in 24:10 and 25:8; the speech that follows is that defense.

records.source: Περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, ἥγημαι ἐμαυτὸν μακάριον ἐπὶ σοῦ μέλλων σήμερον ἀπολογεῖσθαι, μάλιστα γνώστην ὄντα σε πάντων τῶν κατὰ Ἰουδαίους ἐθῶν τε καὶ ζητημάτων· διὸ δέομαι μακροθύμως ἀκοῦσαί μου.
records.gloss: Concerning all of which I am accused by Jews, King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate before you being about today to make a defense, \v 3 especially you being an expert of all the among Jews customs and also controversies; therefore I beg patiently to hear me.
pieces: "King Agrippa, I count myself fortunate that it is before you that I am to answer today for all the charges some Jews bring against me,
especially as you know well all the customs and disputed questions of the Jews. So I ask you to hear me out with patience.

L.2: "Concerning all the things of which I am accused by Jews, King Agrippa, I consider myself fortunate that I am about to make [my] defense before you today,
L.3: especially because you are an expert in all the customs and also controversies among Jews. Therefore I beg [you] to hear me patiently.

R.2: "King Agrippa, some Jewish leaders have brought charges against me. I am glad that today I can answer them in front of you.
R.3: You know all about Jewish customs and the things Jews argue about. So please be patient and listen to me.

decisions.choice: by Jews: by some Jews, without the article
alternatives: by the Jews as a people
decisions.reason: There is no article. Paul is himself a Jew (26:4-5), and his accusers are the leaders from Jerusalem (25:2, 25:7). He uses the same form in 26:7 and 26:21.

decisions.choice: an expert in Jewish customs and disputes
decisions.reason: Agrippa II was raised in Rome but had charge of the temple and appointed the high priests, as Josephus records. He knew the questions that divided Pharisees and Sadducees, such as the resurrection (23:6-8).

decisions.choice: I consider myself fortunate: a courteous opening
decisions.reason: Speakers opened by praising the judge (24:2-4, 24:10). Paul's reason is real: Agrippa knows the Jewish questions, as Festus does not (25:19-20, 25:26).

decisions.choice: King Agrippa placed first
alternatives: in the middle, as in the Greek
decisions.reason: English opens an address with the name; Literal keeps the Greek order.

decisions.choice: some Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Readable names who the accusers were (25:2, 25:7), as the meaning note explains.

records.source: Τὴν μὲν οὖν βίωσίν μου τὴν ἐκ νεότητος τὴν ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς γενομένην ἐν τῷ ἔθνει μου ἔν τε Ἱεροσολύμοις ἴσασι πάντες Ἰουδαῖοι, προγινώσκοντές με ἄνωθεν, ἐὰν θέλωσι μαρτυρεῖν, ὅτι κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεστάτην αἵρεσιν τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας ἔζησα Φαρισαῖος.
records.gloss: The indeed then manner of life of me, the from youth, the from beginning having been among the nation of me and in Jerusalem, know all Jews, \v 5 knowing me before from the first, if they would be willing to testify, that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived [as] a Pharisee.
pieces: All Jews know how I have lived from my youth, from the very start of my life among my own people and in Jerusalem.
They have known me a long time, and if they were willing they could testify that I lived as a Pharisee, in the strictest sect of our religion.

L.4: My manner of life, then, from [my] youth, which from [the] beginning was spent among my own nation and in Jerusalem, all Jews know,
L.5: since they have known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived [as] a Pharisee.

R.4: All the Jews know how I have lived ever since I was young. From the start I lived among my own people and in Jerusalem.
R.5: They have known me for a long time. If they wanted to, they could tell you that I was a Pharisee. The Pharisees are the strictest group in our religion, and I lived by their rules.

decisions.choice: nation: Paul's own people, the Jews
decisions.reason: The same word means "Gentiles" in 26:17, 26:20 and 26:23. Here, with "my", it means his own people, as in 24:17 and 28:19.

decisions.choice: from the first: from long ago
decisions.reason: The word can mean "from above", but with "knowing me before" it means a long time back.

decisions.choice: the strictest sect: the Pharisees
decisions.reason: Josephus also calls the Pharisees the most exact interpreters of the law. Paul was trained under Gamaliel (22:3) and was a son of Pharisees (23:6; Philippians 3:5).

decisions.choice: religion: the outward practice of worship
decisions.reason: The word is used of worship and religious rites (James 1:26-27).

decisions.choice: The Pharisees are the strictest group in our religion, and I lived by their rules
alternatives: according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived as a Pharisee
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the Pharisees were in a short sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: the object first, as in the Greek
alternatives: all Jews know my manner of life
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order; Balanced and Readable begin with the subject.

records.source: καὶ νῦν ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι τῆς εἰς τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν ἐπαγγελίας γενομένης ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἕστηκα κρινόμενος, εἰς ἣν τὸ δωδεκάφυλον ἡμῶν ἐν ἐκτενείᾳ νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν λατρεῦον ἐλπίζει καταντῆσαι· περὶ ἧς ἐλπίδος ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων, βασιλεῦ·
records.gloss: And now for [the] hope of the to the fathers of us promise having been made by the God I stand being judged, \v 7 to which the twelve tribes of us in earnestness night and day serving hope to attain; concerning which hope I am accused by Jews, O king.
pieces: And now I stand on trial because of my hope in the promise God made to our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.
It is the promise our twelve tribes hope to see fulfilled as they worship God with devotion night and day. It is for this hope, Your Majesty, that I am accused by Jews.

L.6: And now I stand being judged for [the] hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,
L.7: to which our twelve tribes, serving [God] earnestly night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope I am accused by Jews, O king.

R.6: And now I am on trial because I hope for what God promised our {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}.
R.7: All twelve tribes of our people worship God day and night, hoping to see that promise come true. Your Majesty, it is because of this hope that some Jewish leaders accuse me.

decisions.choice: the hope: the promise that God will raise the dead
alternatives: the hope of a Messiah in general
decisions.reason: Paul names the hope in 26:8: God raises the dead. He said the same before the council (23:6) and Felix (24:15), and calls it "the hope of Israel" in 28:20.

decisions.choice: the twelve tribes: all Israel
alternatives: only the tribes still in the land
decisions.reason: Paul speaks of the whole people as twelve tribes, though most of the northern tribes had long been scattered (James 1:1; Luke 22:30).

decisions.choice: serving: worshiping God
decisions.reason: The verb is used of worship, especially in the temple (Luke 2:37).

decisions.choice: O king: a respectful address to Agrippa
decisions.reason: Paul addresses Agrippa again in 26:13, 26:19 and 26:27.

decisions.choice: ancestors, with "fathers" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means forebears; Literal keeps the Greek word.

decisions.choice: Your Majesty
decisions.reason: The modern form of address to a king; Literal keeps "O king".

decisions.choice: some Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: As in 26:2: the accusers were the leaders from Jerusalem (25:2, 25:7).

records.source: τί ἄπιστον κρίνεται παρ’ ὑμῖν εἰ ὁ θεὸς νεκροὺς ἐγείρει;
records.gloss: Why incredible is it judged by you if the God [the] dead raises?
pieces: Why do any of you think it unbelievable that God raises the dead?

L.8: Why is it judged incredible by you that God raises [the] dead?

R.8: Why do you think it is impossible for God to bring dead people back to life?

decisions.choice: you: plural, the whole audience
decisions.reason: The pronoun is plural. Paul turns from the king to everyone present, and through them to the Jews who reject the resurrection.

decisions.choice: if: that, stating a fact
decisions.reason: After a verb of judging, "if" introduces the thing judged. Paul does not doubt that God raises the dead.

decisions.choice: impossible
decisions.reason: A plainer word for something that cannot be believed to happen.

records.source: Ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἔδοξα ἐμαυτῷ πρὸς τὸ ὄνομα Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου δεῖν πολλὰ ἐναντία πρᾶξαι·
records.gloss: I indeed therefore thought in myself against the name of Jesus the Nazarene I ought many things contrary to do,
pieces: I myself was once convinced that I had to do all I could to oppose the name of Jesus of Nazareth,

L.9: I myself, then, thought that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus the Nazarene,

R.9: I used to think that I had to fight hard against Jesus from Nazareth and everything his name stood for.

decisions.choice: the name of Jesus: Jesus himself and those who call on him
decisions.reason: The name stands for the person and his authority, as in 3:16 and 4:12. Paul opposed the people who called on the name (9:14, 9:21).

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into 26:10
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the clause with a raised dot; 26:10 begins "which I also did", so the two belong together.

decisions.choice: fight hard against Jesus from Nazareth and everything his name stood for
alternatives: do many things against the name of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable explains what acting against the name meant.

records.source: ὃ καὶ ἐποίησα ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις, καὶ πολλούς τε τῶν ἁγίων ἐγὼ ἐν φυλακαῖς κατέκλεισα τὴν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων ἐξουσίαν λαβών, ἀναιρουμένων τε αὐτῶν κατήνεγκα ψῆφον, καὶ κατὰ πάσας τὰς συναγωγὰς πολλάκις τιμωρῶν αὐτοὺς ἠνάγκαζον βλασφημεῖν, περισσῶς τε ἐμμαινόμενος αὐτοῖς ἐδίωκον ἕως καὶ εἰς τὰς ἔξω πόλεις.
records.gloss: which also I did in Jerusalem, and many also of the saints I in prisons locked up, the from the chief priests authority having received, being put to death then they I cast against a vote, \v 11 and in all the synagogues often punishing them I was compelling to blaspheme, exceedingly then being furious against them I kept persecuting even as far as to the foreign cities.
pieces: and that is what I did in Jerusalem. With authority from the chief priests I shut up many of God's holy people in prison, and when they were condemned to die, I cast my vote against them.
Again and again I had them punished in all the synagogues and tried to force them to blaspheme. My rage against them knew no bounds, and I hunted them down even in cities beyond our land.

L.10: which I also did in Jerusalem. And I locked up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and when they were being put to death, I cast [my] vote against [them].
L.11: And punishing them often in all the synagogues, I was compelling [them] to blaspheme, and being exceedingly furious against them, I kept persecuting [them] even as far as to foreign cities.

R.10: And that is what I did in Jerusalem. The chief priests gave me the right to put many of God's people in prison. When they were sentenced to death, I voted against them.
R.11: I went from one synagogue to another, and many times I had them punished. I tried to make them speak against Jesus. I was so angry with them that I chased them even to cities in other countries.

decisions.choice: the saints: the believers, the people set apart for God
decisions.reason: Ananias uses the same word for the believers in Jerusalem (9:13). It means all who belong to God.

decisions.choice: I cast my vote: Paul gave his approval to their death sentences
alternatives: Paul was a voting member of the council
decisions.reason: The words mean dropping a voting pebble. They may mean Paul sat on a council that voted, or only that he supported the sentences. Acts tells of Stephen's death, at which Paul approved (8:1, 22:20), and of Paul breathing threats and murder (9:1).

decisions.choice: I was compelling them: I tried to force them
decisions.reason: The verb is in the imperfect, which often describes an action attempted or repeated. Acts does not say that any believer gave way.

decisions.choice: to blaspheme: to speak against Jesus
decisions.reason: Paul is persecuting those who call on the name of Jesus (26:9). Pliny the Younger, governor of Bithynia, records making accused Christians curse Christ.

decisions.choice: foreign cities: cities outside the land of Israel
decisions.reason: Damascus, in Syria, is the example that follows (26:12).

decisions.choice: God's holy people (Balanced), God's people (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Saints" now suggests especially holy people; Balanced and Readable say what the word means. Literal keeps "saints".

decisions.choice: speak against Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the word means here, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: I had them punished
decisions.reason: Synagogue punishment, such as flogging, was carried out by the synagogue's officers (Luke 21:12; 2 Corinthians 11:24); Paul arranged it.

records.source: Ἐν οἷς πορευόμενος εἰς τὴν Δαμασκὸν μετ’ ἐξουσίας καὶ ἐπιτροπῆς τῆς τῶν ἀρχιερέων ἡμέρας μέσης κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν εἶδον, βασιλεῦ, οὐρανόθεν ὑπὲρ τὴν λαμπρότητα τοῦ ἡλίου περιλάμψαν με φῶς καὶ τοὺς σὺν ἐμοὶ πορευομένους·
records.gloss: During which journeying to Damascus with authority and commission of the chief priests, \v 13 at mid day on the road I saw, O king, from heaven above the brightness of the sun having shone around me a light and those with me journeying.
pieces: That was my mission when I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests.
At noon, Your Majesty, as I traveled along the road, I saw a light from heaven, brighter than the sun, blazing around me and the men traveling with me.

L.12: While [I was] journeying to Damascus in this [work] with [the] authority and commission of the chief priests,
L.13: at midday on the road I saw, O king, a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining around me and those journeying with me.

R.12: On one of those trips I was going to Damascus. The chief priests had given me the power and the orders to arrest believers there.
R.13: Your Majesty, it was noon, and I was on the road. Suddenly I saw a light from the sky. It was brighter than the sun, and it shone all around me and the men who were with me.

decisions.choice: during which: while carrying out this persecution
decisions.reason: The words look back to the persecution of 26:10-11: the journey was part of it.

decisions.choice: authority and commission: the power and the written orders to act
decisions.reason: The first word is the right to act, the second the charge given; the letters of 9:2 and 22:5 carried both.

decisions.choice: a light from heaven brighter than the sun: the glory of the risen Jesus
decisions.reason: At midday the sun is at its brightest, yet this light outshone it. Paul later says he saw the Lord (26:16; 1 Corinthians 9:1, 15:8).

decisions.choice: from heaven: from the sky, the place of God
decisions.reason: The word can mean either; here the light comes from God's presence.

decisions.choice: to arrest believers there
decisions.reason: Readable states the purpose of the journey, given in 9:2 and 22:5.

decisions.choice: Your Majesty
decisions.reason: As at 26:7.

records.heading: A light from heaven on the road to Damascus

records.source: πάντων τε καταπεσόντων ἡμῶν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἤκουσα φωνὴν λέγουσαν πρός με τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ· Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;
records.gloss: All and having fallen down of us to the ground I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language: Saul, Saul, why me persecute you?
pieces: We all fell to the ground, and I heard a voice speaking to me in Hebrew: 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

L.14: And when we had all fallen down to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew language, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

R.14: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice speak to me in my own language. It said, 'Saul, Saul, why are you hurting {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

decisions.choice: the Hebrew language: the language of the Jews of the land, probably Aramaic
alternatives: Hebrew, the language of the Scriptures
decisions.reason: The phrase covers the Semitic speech of the Jews in Judea. In Paul's day that was mostly Aramaic, though Hebrew was still used. Only this telling of the story mentions the language.

decisions.choice: Saul: the Hebrew form of the name
decisions.reason: Here, as in 9:4 and 22:7, the voice uses the Hebrew form of the name, which fits a voice speaking Hebrew.

decisions.choice: persecuting me: Jesus is one with his followers
decisions.reason: Paul attacked believers, and the risen Jesus counts it as done to himself (9:4-5; Luke 10:16).

decisions.choice: in my own language
decisions.reason: Readable avoids settling between Hebrew and Aramaic, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: hurting
decisions.reason: A plainer word for persecuting.

records.source: σκληρόν σοι πρὸς κέντρα λακτίζειν.
records.gloss: [It is] hard for you against goads to kick.
pieces: It hurts you to kick against the goads.'

L.14: [It is] hard for you to kick against [the] goads.'

R.14: You are only hurting yourself by fighting against me, like an ox kicking against a farmer's pointed stick.'

decisions.choice: kicking against the goads: a Greek proverb for useless resistance
decisions.reason: A goad was a pointed stick used to drive an ox; an ox that kicked back only drove it into itself. The saying is found in Greek writers such as Euripides. It belongs to this telling of the story only.

decisions.choice: it hurts you: resisting the Lord is useless and harms the one who resists
alternatives: Paul's conscience was already troubling him
decisions.reason: The proverb is about the useless struggle of the animal, not about its inner feelings. Paul says elsewhere that he acted in ignorance (1 Timothy 1:13).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: the proverb only here
alternatives: some later manuscripts also add it in 9:5
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add the proverb to 9:5 as well, copying it from here. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: it hurts you
decisions.reason: The word means hard in the sense of painful for the one who kicks.

decisions.choice: You are only hurting yourself by fighting against me, like an ox kicking against a farmer's pointed stick
alternatives: It is hard for you to kick against the goads
decisions.reason: Readable explains the proverb, as the meaning notes do.

records.source: ἐγὼ δὲ εἶπα· Τίς εἶ, κύριε;
records.gloss: I then said: Who are you, Lord?
pieces: I asked, 'Who are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, Lord?'

decisions.choice: Lord: a title of respect to one Paul does not yet know
alternatives: a confession that he is God
decisions.reason: Paul does not yet know who speaks, but he knows it is a heavenly voice. The narrator then calls the speaker "the Lord" (26:15).

records.source: ὁ δὲ κύριος εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις·
records.gloss: And the Lord said: I am Jesus whom you are persecuting.
pieces: The Lord answered, 'I am Jesus, the one you are persecuting.

L.15: And the Lord said, 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.

R.15: The Lord said, 'I am Jesus. I am the one you are hurting.

decisions.choice: I am Jesus: the one Paul persecuted is alive and Lord
decisions.reason: The same words as 9:5 and 22:8. Paul later counts this as a true appearance of the risen Lord (1 Corinthians 15:8).

decisions.choice: hurting
decisions.reason: As in 26:14.

records.source: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ στῆθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου· εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ὤφθην σοι, προχειρίσασθαί σε ὑπηρέτην καὶ μάρτυρα ὧν τε εἶδές με ὧν τε ὀφθήσομαί σοι, ἐξαιρούμενός σε ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἐθνῶν, εἰς οὓς ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω σε ἀνοῖξαι ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν, τοῦ ἐπιστρέψαι ἀπὸ σκότους εἰς φῶς καὶ τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, τοῦ λαβεῖν αὐτοὺς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ κλῆρον ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πίστει τῇ εἰς ἐμέ.
records.gloss: But rise up and stand on the feet of you; for this purpose for I have appeared to you, to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things you have seen me and of the things I will appear to you, \v 17 delivering you out from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am sending you \v 18 to open eyes of them, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those having been sanctified by faith that [is] in me.
pieces: But rise, stand up on your feet. I have shown myself to you for a purpose: to choose you as my assistant and my witness, to tell what you have seen of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and what I will yet show you of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
I will keep you safe from your own people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to them

to open their eyes, so that they turn from darkness to light and from Satan's power to God, and so receive forgiveness of their sins and a share in the inheritance among those sanctified by faith in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

L.16: But rise up and stand on your feet, for I have appeared to you for this purpose, to appoint you a servant and a witness both of the things in which you have seen {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and of the things in which I will appear to you,
L.17: delivering you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am sending you
L.18: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, so that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those sanctified by faith in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

R.16: Now get up and stand on your feet. I have come to you because I have chosen you to work for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You will tell people what you have seen of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and what I will show you later.
R.17: I will protect you from the Jewish people and from the Gentiles. I am sending you to the Gentiles
R.18: to open their eyes. Then they can turn away from darkness and come into the light. They can turn away from the power of Satan and come to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and they will receive a share with all God's people, who are made holy by faith in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.'

decisions.choice: stand on your feet: the words of a prophet's call
alternatives: only a command to get up
decisions.reason: God says the same to Ezekiel at his call (Ezekiel 2:1). The whole commission echoes the prophets.

decisions.choice: rescuing you ... to whom I am sending you: the call of Jeremiah
decisions.reason: God tells Jeremiah, "To all to whom I send you, you shall go," and, "I am with you to rescue you" (Jeremiah 1:7-8).

decisions.choice: delivering: rescuing you from danger
alternatives: choosing you out from among them
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to rescue or to pick out. Rescue matches Jeremiah 1:8 and Paul's rescues in Acts (23:27). "Choosing" would match his being set apart from his people (9:15).

decisions.choice: to open their eyes, from darkness to light: Isaiah's servant
decisions.reason: God's servant is sent "to open eyes that are blind" and to lead people out of darkness (Isaiah 42:7, 42:16), and to be a light for the nations (Isaiah 49:6). Paul applies this to himself in 13:47.

decisions.choice: the people: Israel
decisions.reason: The word is used for Israel as God's people, set beside "the Gentiles".

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "you have seen me"
alternatives: some manuscripts lack "me": "what you have seen"
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts leave out "me"; others include it. The sense is close either way. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: by faith in me: goes with "sanctified"
alternatives: goes with the whole sentence: they receive forgiveness by faith in me
decisions.reason: The phrase stands right after "sanctified" and most naturally tells how they are made holy. Either way, faith in Jesus is the means.

decisions.choice: an inheritance among the sanctified: a share with God's people
decisions.reason: As Israel received a share of the land, so believers receive a share with those God has set apart for himself (20:32; Colossians 1:12).

decisions.choice: servant: an assistant who carries out another's orders
decisions.reason: This is not the word for slave; it is used of an assistant or attendant, such as John Mark (13:5) and those who serve the word (Luke 1:2).

decisions.choice: assistant (Balanced); work for me (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word is for one who serves under orders, not a slave; Literal keeps "servant".

decisions.choice: I am sending you to the Gentiles
alternatives: to whom I am sending you
decisions.reason: Readable names the nearer group as those to whom Paul is sent, as Paul's own mission shows (22:21).

decisions.choice: their sins will be forgiven
decisions.reason: Readable turns the noun into a plain verb.

records.source: Ὅθεν, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, οὐκ ἐγενόμην ἀπειθὴς τῇ οὐρανίῳ ὀπτασίᾳ, ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἐν Δαμασκῷ πρῶτόν τε καὶ Ἱεροσολύμοις, πᾶσάν τε τὴν χώραν τῆς Ἰουδαίας, καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπήγγελλον μετανοεῖν καὶ ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, ἄξια τῆς μετανοίας ἔργα πράσσοντας.
records.gloss: So then, O king Agrippa, not I was disobedient to the heavenly vision, \v 20 but to those in Damascus first both and in Jerusalem, all and the region of Judea, and to the Gentiles I kept declaring to repent and to turn to God, worthy of repentance works doing.
pieces: And so, King Agrippa, I did not resist the heavenly vision.

I went first to the people of Damascus, then to Jerusalem and the whole country of Judea, and to the Gentiles too, and I told them all to repent and turn to God, and to live in a way that proves their repentance.

L.19: So then, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
L.20: but to those in Damascus first, and in Jerusalem, and [throughout] all the region of Judea, and to the Gentiles, I kept declaring that [they should] repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.

R.19: So, King Agrippa, I obeyed what God showed me in that vision from heaven.
R.20: First I preached to the people in Damascus. Then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea, and to the Gentiles as well. I told them all to stop sinning and turn to God. I told them to show by what they did that they had really changed.

decisions.choice: not disobedient: fully obedient
decisions.reason: Saying "not disobedient" is a modest way to say Paul obeyed at once (9:20).

decisions.choice: all the region of Judea: throughout Judea
alternatives: to all the people of Judea
decisions.reason: The phrase stands without a preposition, which is awkward. It probably means throughout Judea. Acts tells little of such a mission (9:28-29), so the words may sum up Paul's work among Jews in general.

decisions.choice: works worthy of repentance: the call of John the Baptist
decisions.reason: John told the crowds to bear fruit worthy of repentance (Luke 3:8).

decisions.choice: repent: turn away from sin and change one's mind and life
decisions.reason: The word means a change of mind that leads to a changed life, as the rest of the verse shows.

decisions.choice: I did not resist
decisions.reason: A natural English way to keep the negative.

decisions.choice: I obeyed
decisions.reason: Readable says the positive meaning, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: stop sinning and turn to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what repentance means.

records.source: ἕνεκα τούτων με Ἰουδαῖοι συλλαβόμενοι ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐπειρῶντο διαχειρίσασθαι.
records.gloss: On account of these things me Jews having seized in the temple were attempting to kill.
pieces: It was for this that some Jews seized me in the temple and set about murdering me.

L.21: On account of these things Jews seized me in the temple and were attempting to kill [me].

R.21: That is why some Jews grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.

decisions.choice: these things: Paul's preaching, above all to Gentiles
decisions.reason: The charge against him was that he taught against the people and the law, and brought Greeks into the temple (21:28).

decisions.choice: seized in the temple: the riot of 21:27-31
decisions.reason: A crowd dragged Paul out of the temple and was trying to kill him until the tribune intervened (21:30-32).

decisions.choice: Jews: some Jews, without the article
decisions.reason: As in 26:2: those who seized him were Jews from Asia (21:27).

decisions.choice: some Jews
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "some" to show that the Greek has no article.

records.source: ἐπικουρίας οὖν τυχὼν τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης ἕστηκα μαρτυρόμενος μικρῷ τε καὶ μεγάλῳ, οὐδὲν ἐκτὸς λέγων ὧν τε οἱ προφῆται ἐλάλησαν μελλόντων γίνεσθαι καὶ Μωϋσῆς, εἰ παθητὸς ὁ χριστός, εἰ πρῶτος ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν φῶς μέλλει καταγγέλλειν τῷ τε λαῷ καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.
records.gloss: Help therefore having obtained from God until the day this I have stood bearing witness to small both and to great, nothing other saying than what both the prophets said was about to happen and Moses, \v 23 that would suffer the Christ, that first through resurrection from dead light he is about to proclaim to both the people and to the Gentiles.
pieces: God has helped me, and up to this very day I stand here bearing witness to people of low and high rank alike. I say only what the prophets and Moses foretold:
that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} must suffer, and that, as the first to rise from the dead, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would announce light both to our own people and to the Gentiles."

L.22: So, having obtained help from God, I have stood until this day bearing witness to both small and great, saying nothing other than what the prophets and Moses said was about to happen:
L.23: that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} must suffer, [and] that, [being the] first from [the] resurrection of [the] dead, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is about to proclaim light both to the people and to the Gentiles."

R.22: But God has helped me, and I am still here today. I tell my story to everyone, poor and powerful. I say only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
R.23: They said the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} must suffer and die. He would be the first to rise from the dead. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would bring the light of God's message to the Jewish people and to the Gentiles."

decisions.choice: small and great: everyone, humble and important alike
decisions.reason: The pair means people of every rank; Paul now speaks before a king and a governor.

decisions.choice: I have stood bearing witness: I have kept on testifying
decisions.reason: The perfect tense looks at his whole witness up to this day, including the present hearing.

decisions.choice: that ... that: the points the Scriptures foretold
alternatives: whether ... whether: open questions for debate
decisions.reason: The word usually means "if". After "what the prophets said" it lists the points Paul showed from Scripture, perhaps as the questions under debate with Jews.

decisions.choice: must suffer: destined to suffer, including death
decisions.reason: The word means subject to suffering. In context it is what the prophets foretold (3:18; Luke 24:26, 24:46).

decisions.choice: the Christ: the title, the Anointed One promised by God
decisions.reason: With the article the word is a title here, as in 17:3: the point to be shown is that the Messiah must suffer.

decisions.choice: first from the resurrection of the dead: the first to rise to new life
alternatives: the first of all ever raised
decisions.reason: Others had been brought back to life and died again. Jesus is the first to rise never to die again, the firstfruits of all who will be raised (1 Corinthians 15:20; Colossians 1:18).

decisions.choice: light to the people and to the Gentiles: Isaiah's servant
decisions.reason: The servant of the Lord is "a light for the nations" (Isaiah 42:6, 49:6), words Simeon used of Jesus (Luke 2:32).

decisions.choice: our own people (Balanced), the Jewish people (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means Israel, set beside the Gentiles; Literal keeps "the people".

decisions.choice: the light of God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says what the light is: the message of salvation the Messiah proclaims through his witnesses (13:47).

decisions.choice: suffer and die
decisions.reason: Readable says what the suffering included, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀπολογουμένου ὁ Φῆστος μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ φησιν· Μαίνῃ, Παῦλε· τὰ πολλά σε γράμματα εἰς μανίαν περιτρέπει.
records.gloss: These things now of him saying in his defense, the Festus in a loud voice says: You are insane, Paul; the great of you learning to insanity turns.
pieces: As Paul was saying this in his defense, Festus called out loudly, "You are out of your mind, Paul! All your great learning is pushing you into madness."

L.24: Now as he was saying these things in his defense, Festus says in a loud voice, "You are out of your mind, Paul; your great learning is turning you to madness."

R.24: While Paul was still speaking, Festus shouted, "Paul, you are out of your mind! All your studying has made you crazy."

decisions.choice: you are insane: you are out of your mind
alternatives: you are inspired, in a frenzy
decisions.reason: Festus means that Paul's talk of a risen man and a light from heaven sounds like madness. He had called the resurrection a dispute about "a certain dead man Jesus" (25:19).

decisions.choice: your great learning: your study of books, probably the Jewish Scriptures
decisions.reason: The word means letters or writings, and so education. Paul has been arguing from the prophets and Moses (26:22).

decisions.choice: says: present tense, telling the moment vividly
decisions.reason: Luke uses the present tense for vividness; it means "said". Literal keeps the present.

decisions.choice: called out (Balanced), shouted (Readable)
decisions.reason: English tells a past event in the past tense; the loud voice is in the verb.

decisions.choice: all your studying
decisions.reason: A plainer phrase for the same thing.

records.heading: Festus interrupts, and Paul appeals to the king

records.source: ὁ δὲ Παῦλος· Οὐ μαίνομαι, φησίν, κράτιστε Φῆστε, ἀλλὰ ἀληθείας καὶ σωφροσύνης ῥήματα ἀποφθέγγομαι.
records.gloss: But Paul: Not I am insane, says he, most excellent Festus, but of truth and sobriety words I utter.
pieces: "I am not mad, most excellent Festus," Paul replied. "The words I am speaking are truth and sound sense.

L.25: But Paul [said], "I am not out of my mind," he says, "most excellent Festus, but I am uttering words of truth and sober sense.

R.25: Paul answered, "Most excellent Festus, I am not out of my mind. What I am saying is the truth, and it makes good sense.

decisions.choice: most excellent: the formal title for a Roman governor
decisions.reason: Paul gave Felix the same title (23:26, 24:3), as Luke does Theophilus (Luke 1:3). Paul answers Festus with full courtesy.

decisions.choice: truth and sober sense: what is true and what is sane
decisions.reason: The second word means a sound, self-controlled mind, the opposite of the madness Festus charged (26:24).

decisions.choice: utter: speak out clearly and deliberately
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the apostles speaking at Pentecost (2:4, 2:14); here it means plain and serious speech.

decisions.choice: Paul's reply placed around the address
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order, with "he says" inside the speech; Balanced and Readable use English order.

records.source: ἐπίσταται γὰρ περὶ τούτων ὁ βασιλεύς, πρὸς ὃν καὶ παρρησιαζόμενος λαλῶ· λανθάνειν γὰρ αὐτὸν τούτων οὐ πείθομαι οὐθέν, οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἐν γωνίᾳ πεπραγμένον τοῦτο.
records.gloss: Understands for concerning these things the king, to whom also using boldness I speak; are hidden from for him of these things not I am persuaded none, not for is in a corner done this.
pieces: The king understands these matters, and that is why I can speak to him so openly. I am sure that nothing of this has passed him by. After all, it did not happen in some out-of-the-way corner.

L.26: For the king understands about these things, to whom I also speak boldly; for I am not persuaded that any of these things is hidden from him, for this has not been done in a corner.

R.26: King Agrippa knows about these things, so I can speak to him freely. I am sure he has heard about all of them. These things did not happen in secret.

decisions.choice: not done in a corner: done in public, where all could see
decisions.reason: The phrase was a Greek saying for something hidden. Jesus's death and resurrection and the spread of the church were public events in Jerusalem (Luke 24:18).

decisions.choice: not persuaded that any is hidden: sure that none is hidden
decisions.reason: The double negative is a strong way to say Paul is confident.

decisions.choice: using boldness: speaking freely and openly
decisions.reason: The word is used for the apostles' open speech (4:13, 4:29).

decisions.choice: did not happen in secret
alternatives: was not done in a corner
decisions.reason: Readable explains the saying, as the meaning note does.

decisions.choice: King Agrippa
decisions.reason: Readable names the king, since Paul speaks of him to Festus.

records.source: πιστεύεις, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, τοῖς προφήταις;
records.gloss: Believe you, King Agrippa, the prophets?
pieces: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets?

L.27: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets?

R.27: King Agrippa, do you believe what the prophets wrote?

decisions.choice: believe the prophets: accept that their words are true and from God
decisions.reason: A Jewish king would accept the prophets as Scripture. Paul has argued that they foretold the Messiah's death and resurrection (26:22-23).

decisions.choice: what the prophets wrote
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that he means their writings.

records.source: οἶδα ὅτι πιστεύεις.
records.gloss: I know that you believe.
pieces: I know that you believe them."

R.27: I know that you believe it."

decisions.choice: I know that you believe: Paul answers his own question
alternatives: a question for Agrippa to answer
decisions.reason: Paul gives the answer himself, which puts Agrippa in a hard place: to deny it would offend his Jewish subjects; to agree would seem to grant Paul's case.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἀγρίππας πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον· Ἐν ὀλίγῳ με πείθεις Χριστιανὸν ποιῆσαι.
records.gloss: Then Agrippa [said] to Paul: In little me you persuade a Christian to make.
pieces: Agrippa said to Paul, "In so short a time you are persuading me to become a Christian!"

L.28: Then Agrippa [said] to Paul, "In a short time you are persuading me to become a Christian."

R.28: Agrippa said to Paul, "So in this short time you think you can make me a Christian!"

decisions.choice: a statement, probably spoken with irony
alternatives: a question: Do you think that in a short time you can persuade me?
a sincere admission that he is nearly persuaded
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT prints a statement. Agrippa is turning aside Paul's question (26:27) without answering it. It may be a mocking question instead. The old reading "Almost you persuade me" takes it as sincere, but the phrase does not mean "almost".

decisions.choice: in a short time: so quickly, with so little
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean in a short time or with little effort. Paul takes it up in 26:29 with "in little and in much".

decisions.choice: to make me a Christian: to persuade me to become a Christian
alternatives: to persuade me to play the part of a Christian
decisions.reason: The verb is "make", which is hard here. It may mean "you are persuading me so as to make me a Christian", or "you are persuading me to act the Christian" in front of this audience.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "to make"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, read "to become", an easier wording. Early manuscripts read "to make". Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Christian: the name outsiders gave Jesus's followers
decisions.reason: The name was first used in Antioch (11:26) and appears only once more in the New Testament (1 Peter 4:16).

decisions.choice: become a Christian (Balanced); make me a Christian (Readable)
decisions.reason: Both keep the sense chosen in the meaning notes; Readable keeps the Greek verb "make".

decisions.choice: an exclamation, to show the irony
decisions.reason: The punctuation shows the irony the meaning note describes; Literal keeps a plain statement.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Παῦλος· Εὐξαίμην ἂν τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐν ὀλίγῳ καὶ ἐν μεγάλῳ οὐ μόνον σὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντάς μου σήμερον γενέσθαι τοιούτους ὁποῖος καὶ ἐγώ εἰμι παρεκτὸς τῶν δεσμῶν τούτων.
records.gloss: And Paul [said]: I would wish to God, both in little and in great, not only you but also all those hearing me this day to become such as also I am, except the chains these.
pieces: Paul answered, "Whether it takes little or much, my prayer to God is that not you alone but every one of my hearers today would come to be as I am, though without these chains."

L.29: And Paul [said], "I would pray to God that, both in little and in much, not only you but also all who hear me today might become such as I also am, except for these chains."

R.29: Paul answered, "Whether it takes a little or a lot, I pray to God for you. I pray that you and everyone listening to me today will become like me, a follower of Jesus. But I would not want you to wear chains like these!"

decisions.choice: in little and in much: whether it takes little or much
alternatives: in a short or a long time
decisions.reason: Paul takes up Agrippa's "in little" (26:28). "Much" suits effort or degree more than time, but both are possible.

decisions.choice: I would pray: a polite wish
decisions.reason: The form expresses a wish courteously; it means "my prayer would be".

decisions.choice: such as I am: believers in Jesus
decisions.reason: Paul wants them to share his faith, not his chains, as the closing words show.

decisions.choice: a follower of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says what Paul means by "such as I am", as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: But I would not want you to wear chains like these
decisions.reason: Readable turns the phrase into a short sentence.

records.source: Ἀνέστη τε ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἥ τε Βερνίκη καὶ οἱ συγκαθήμενοι αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἀναχωρήσαντες ἐλάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες ὅτι Οὐδὲν θανάτου ἢ δεσμῶν ἄξιον τι πράσσει ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος.
records.gloss: Rose up then the king and the governor and Bernice and those sitting with them, \v 31 and having withdrawn they began speaking to one another saying, Nothing of death or chains worthy anything is doing the man this.
pieces: Then the king stood up, with the governor, Bernice and those seated with them.
After they had gone out, they said to each other, "Nothing this man does calls for death or prison."

L.30: Then the king rose up, and the governor and Bernice and those sitting with them,
L.31: and having withdrawn, they were speaking to one another, saying, "This man is doing nothing worthy of death or chains."

R.30: Then the king, the governor, Bernice and all the others who were sitting with them got up.
R.31: They left the room and talked together. They said, "This man has not done anything to deserve death or prison."

decisions.choice: the king rose: the sign that the hearing was over
decisions.reason: The one of highest rank rises first, and the others follow.

decisions.choice: Bernice: Agrippa's sister
decisions.reason: Bernice was the sister of Agrippa II and of Drusilla, the wife of Felix (24:24), as Josephus records.

decisions.choice: chains: imprisonment
decisions.reason: Chains stand for being kept a prisoner.

decisions.choice: is doing: Paul's conduct, his way of life
decisions.reason: The present tense looks at how Paul lives and teaches, not only at the charges.

decisions.choice: prison
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what chains stand for, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps "chains".

records.heading: Nothing deserving death or chains

records.source: Ἀγρίππας δὲ τῷ Φήστῳ ἔφη· Ἀπολελύσθαι ἐδύνατο ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος εἰ μὴ ἐπεκέκλητο Καίσαρα.
records.gloss: Agrippa then to Festus said: Have been released could the man this if not he had appealed to Caesar.
pieces: Agrippa told Festus, "This man might have gone free, had he not appealed to Caesar."

L.32: And Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have been released if he had not appealed to Caesar."

R.32: Agrippa said to Festus, "This man could have gone free if he had not asked for his case to be heard by Caesar."

decisions.choice: appealed to Caesar: Paul's right as a Roman citizen to be tried before the emperor
alternatives: a request Festus could simply ignore
decisions.reason: Paul had appealed in 25:11, and Festus had granted it (25:12). Once granted, the case went to Rome; to release him then would have overruled the emperor's court. The emperor was Nero.

decisions.choice: the verdict: Paul is innocent, yet he will go to Rome
decisions.reason: Luke shows each official finding Paul innocent (23:29, 25:25). The Lord had said Paul must testify in Rome (23:11).

decisions.choice: asked for his case to be heard by Caesar
decisions.reason: Readable explains what an appeal was.
